problem: OpenObserve is a cloud-native observability platform. Prior to 1.1.0, the shared authentication validator in src/api/common/src/auth/validator.rs accepts an empty or whitespace-only HTTP Basic password for an account whose password_ext value is missing or empty. SSO-provisioned and migration-created users can have this state, allowing an unauthenticated attacker who knows an affected user's email address and organization to authenticate on protected non-ingestion API routes with the victim's role and permissions. A compromised privileged account can expose or modify telemetry, alerts, streams, users, and security configuration. An account with search permission can submit a DataFusion COPY... TO statement through the search API to create or overwrite attacker-controlled files at service-process-writable locations, creating a conditional escalation to pre-authentication remote code execution. This issue is fixed in version 1.1.0. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Fixed in version 1.1.0 — update immediately. Enforce authentication on every affected endpoint/server-side; do not rely on client checks. Update to the patched version.

problem: Active Storage makes it simple to upload and reference files in cloud services and attach those files to Active Record objects. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, a Rails application that processes attachments with ImageMagick may allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on the server and, when attachments are stored with the Disk service, to read arbitrary files readable by the application process. Those files typically include secret_key_base and credentials for external systems, which may in turn allow escalation to remote code execution or lateral movement to those systems. ImageMagick selects a coder from the content of the file it is given, and some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image itself. Active Storage constrained none of ImageMagick's coders, and the ImageMagick analyzer runs when a file is attached, so an attacker who can upload a crafted file may be able to invoke one. Attaching the upload is sufficient; no variant, preview, or analyze call is required. One specific attack chain has been reported, but other attack chains may exist. An application is affected when it uses ImageMagick for Active Storage image processing through config.active_storage.variant_processor =:mini_magick, runs ImageMagick under a security policy that does not already deny the involved coders, and allows uploads from untrusted users. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Apply the vendor patch at the earliest maintenance window and confirm the asset is not internet-exposed.

problem: The Basel Post Types plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.18. The vulnerability exists because a missing-quotes coding error in the defined() call for SECURE_AUTH_SALT inside BASEL_Auth::get_config() causes PHP to evaluate the constant's value rather than its name, making the check always fail and permanently falling back to the static hardcoded salt 2NlBUibcszrVtNmDnxqDbwCOpLWq91eatIz6O1O that is publicly visible in the theme source code; because this salt is static and known, an attacker can compute a valid Opauth signature entirely offline and submit a forged ?opauth callback to the unauthenticated init hook endpoint processed by register_or_login. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user, including administrators, by forging a callback tied to a known target account email address — bypassing all password verification, multi-factor authentication, and ownership checks, and receiving a fully authenticated session cookie via wc_set_customer_auth_cookie(). Exploitation requires WooCommerce to be active and at least one Basel social-login provider (Facebook, Google, or VKontakte) to be configured with a valid app_id and app_secret in the theme settings. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Enforce authentication on every affected endpoint/server-side; do not rely on client checks. Update to the patched version.

problem: NOsql Object (NO2 a.k.a Nitrite) database is an open source nosql embedded document store. Prior to version 4.4.1, when Nitrite opens a database file, MVStoreUtils.openOrCreate() automatically checks for a legacy v1-format store and, on detecting one (or hitting a compatibility error while opening), triggers an automatic migration path. This path deserializes stored values using NitriteDataType.deserialize(byte[]), which passes the raw bytes directly to java.io.ObjectInputStream.readObject() via a custom NitriteObjectInputStream subclass. That subclass overrides only readClassDescriptor() — solely to remap a handful of known legacy class names to their current equivalents — and implements no class allowlist, blocklist, or ObjectInputFilter (JEP 290). Any Serializable class reachable on the embedding application's classpath can therefore be instantiated via readObject(), with readObject()/readExternal()/readResolve() callbacks invoked unconditionally. If a suitable gadget class (e.g. from commons-collections or similar) happens to be present on the classpath, this is a precondition for remote code execution. This issue has been patched in version 4.4.1. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Fixed in version 4.4.1 — update immediately. Never deserialize untrusted data; require signed/integrity-checked payloads. Update to the patched version.

problem: Waline is a comment system with backend support. In versions 3.15.2 and prior, @waline/client renders the comment editor's live preview with marked and no sanitizer (utils/markdown.ts), and the preview is injected with v-html. When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (orig). Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTML in their own session: an unauthenticated commenter achieves privilege-escalation stored XSS against a moderator with a single Edit click. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches. Exploitable remotely over the network.

problem: HarnessRouter is a self-hosted unified API for running agent harnesses with sessions, streaming, files, cancellation, and failure handling. Prior to 0.31.8, a console that is not in self-hosted mode attaches the server's internal key to requests carrying an Authorization header before validating the bearer, while the service-only PUT and GET /v1/orgs/{org}/connections/{name}, PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/policy/{backend}, and /internal/* routes trust that key and take the organization from the URL. In a multi-organization deployment, a remote caller can use a made-up bearer to rewrite another organization's provider connection to an attacker-controlled endpoint, causing later prompts to be disclosed and attacker-controlled responses to influence tasks. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.8. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Fixed in version 0.31.8 — update immediately. Add server-side authorization checks for every object and action. Update to the patched version.

problem: An issue exists in MongoDB's macOS TLS client implementation where certificate chain-of-trust validation is bypassed for outbound connections to IPv6-addressed peers. When a MongoDB process using the Apple SecureTransport TLS backend connects to an IPv6 target, the trust evaluation result from SecTrustEvaluate is silently discarded, regardless of whether the peer's certificate is trusted. An on-path party could exploit this by presenting a self-signed certificate containing the target's IPv6 address in the Subject Alternative Name to intercept and modify encrypted inter-node or external service traffic. This issue only affects MongoDB processes running on macOS with the Apple SecureTransport TLS provider. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Apply the vendor patch at the earliest maintenance window and confirm the asset is not internet-exposed.

Serving any static file therefore replaced that bounded value with the file's on-disk size, and nothing resets it afterwards. The defect is reached by an unauthenticated HTTP/2 GET for any file under the web root, in applications that register a static-filesystem resource (HTTP_RESOURCE_TYPE_STATIC_FS) with CONFIG_FILE_SYSTEM=y; CONFIG_HTTP_SERVER_VERSION_2 is enabled by default and no TLS or credentials are required on this path. Once client->data_len exceeds the buffer size, the frame dispatch loop in subsys/net/lib/http/http_server_core.c keeps parsing past the end of the received data, and the peer controls the bytes at client->cursor, so it can choose which fabricated frame the state machine consumes next by appending bytes after its request. problem: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and arbitrary file read via S3/Dropbox/Google Drive exfiltration) in versions up to, and including, 3.3.36. The flaw spans NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process() in includes/fields/upload.php — which returns early (leaving the client-supplied files[] intact) whenever a public submission carries a nonempty extra.saveProgress — and NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload() in includes/external/abstracts/service.php, whose authoritative-path reload only fires when the client sends upload_id. By omitting upload_id, an attacker's data[file_path] survives into the Background Upload queue and is used by both upload_file_to_s3() (as SourceFile) and the maybe_delete_server_file() unlink() call in includes/external/abstracts/backgroundupload.php, with no canonicalization or upload-directory containment check (the plugin's own is_path_within_upload_dir() helper is only applied on admin paths). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible — specifically, deleting wp-config.php forces WordPress into its setup screen, enabling full site takeover. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Canonicalize paths and restrict to an allowlisted directory. Update to the patched version.

problem: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signed by a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification. Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass). verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was not affected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor came from the message. This issue has been patched in version 0.13.0. Exploitable remotely over the network.

problem: node-fontnik is a library that delivers a range of glyphs rendered as SDFs (signed distance fields) in a protocol buffer. Prior to version 0.7.7, a crafted font could trigger a heap out-of-bounds write in RenderSDF (include/mapbox/glyph_foundry_impl.hpp). RenderSDF computed the SDF bitmap allocation size as buffered_width * buffered_height in 32-bit unsigned int. Glyph dimensions are derived from the uploaded font's outline bounding box with no upper bound, so a glyph large enough to make that product exceed 2³² wrapped to a small value. The buffer was then under-allocated while the render loop still wrote one byte per pixel, corrupting the heap (CWE-190 → CWE-787) and crashing the process. A 680-byte font is enough to drive FreeType to a 65536×65536 buffered glyph, wrapping the size to 0. This issue has been patched in version 0.7.7. Exploitable remotely over the network.

problem: Affected versions of Git have a heap buffer overflow in the three-way merge code (xdiff), which an attacker can trigger through a repository they control. A small file with a huge marker size and many separate conflicts can therefore push the total past 4 GiB, so the integer wraps to a small value and Git writes attacker-controlled merge output past the end of a buffer that is too small. problem: The Everest Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.3 via the attach_entry_files() function. This is due to the function attaching any entry field value whose meta key matches /signature_/ to the notification email after only a file_exists() check, without validating or restricting the path. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, such as wp-config.php, which can contain sensitive information. Successful exploitation requires a form whose email notification has the “Attach Files” setting enabled and that contains a field with a meta key matching /signature_/ (for example, a text field labelled “Signature”), with the notification routed to an attacker-supplied email address so the exfiltrated file is delivered to the attacker. Note: The Everest Forms Pro add-on is required to exploit this vulnerability, as it provides the signature field and the email file-attachment functionality (file-email-attachments) that the attack relies on. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Canonicalize paths and restrict to an allowlisted directory. Update to the patched version.

problem: Active Support is a collection of utility classes and standard library extensions used by Rails and other Ruby projects. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, when constant lookup raises LoadError, ActiveSupport::Inflector#safe_constantize (and String#safe_constantize) builds a regular expression from the requested constant name without escaping it, so a caller that passes untrusted input lets the attacker choose the source of a pattern that the application compiles. Crafted patterns can trigger defects in Ruby's regular expression compiler, possibly leading to a crash of the server process, and repeated requests could keep the application unavailable. Action Cable passes the channel value of each subscribe command to safe_constantize before any channel lookup, so an unauthenticated client can reach this code when the application mounts Action Cable and accepts connections from untrusted clients without an added authentication check. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2. Exploitable remotely over the network.

problem: Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, ActionController::Parameters#each_key delegates to the internal ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess that holds the request parameters, so when called with a block it returns that hash instead of the Parameters instance. The hash does not respond to permitted?, so Active Model mass assignment (new, assign_attributes, update) accepts it without raising ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesError. An application that passes the return value of each_key to mass assignment could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to set attributes that the application does not permit, such as an authorization flag. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2020-8164, which made each, each_pair and each_value return the Parameters instance but left each_key delegated. An application is affected if it passes the return value of ActionController::Parameters#each_key, called with a block, to mass assignment. Rails itself makes no such call. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2. Exploitable remotely over the network.

problem: pam_usb provides hardware authentication for Linux using removable media. problem: Moby's overlay network driver does not restore the iptables rules for encrypted overlay networks after firewalld deletes them. Unlike other Docker Engine networking components, the overlay driver does not handle firewalld reload or start signals over D-Bus. The missing rules cause outgoing VXLAN datagrams to bypass IPsec encryption and remove the protection against incoming cleartext VXLAN traffic. The condition is not logged by dockerd and persists until the encrypted network's last local endpoint is removed and another is added, or dockerd is restarted. Each further firewalld event repeats the condition. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Apply the vendor patch at the earliest maintenance window and confirm the asset is not internet-exposed.

problem: A flaw in MongoDB Server's user management commands may lead to incomplete cleanup of role authorization data when roles are dropped from a database. Due to incorrect internal query predicates, the drop operation removes role definitions but fails to remove stale references in user and role documents. If a role with the same name is subsequently recreated with different privileges, previously associated users may silently inherit the new role's privileges without an explicit grant or corresponding audit event. Exploitation requires authenticated access with database administrative privileges on the target database. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Apply the vendor patch at the earliest maintenance window and confirm the asset is not internet-exposed.

problem: On affected platforms running Arista EOS with IEEE 802.1X authentication and MACsec using dynamically derived keys, sensitive authentication information may be recorded in diagnostic data during a Smart Switch Upgrade (SSU). This could potentially compromise the confidentiality and integrity of traffic protected by MACsec on the affected link. The vulnerability is only exposed during and after an SSU reload where an active 802.1X session used for MACsec is present. Requires local access to exploit.

problem: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.3.4 through 6.3.7, with a MySQL or MariaDB database, TlsMode=verify-full and no TlsCaFile, does not verify the database server's certificate's issuer or name when the connection is one that MariaDB Connector/C treats as local - Server= set to 127.0.0.1,::1 or localhost (on Linux a Unix socket), to. on Windows (a named pipe), or to a comma-separated list of servers that holds such an element - which allows a local attacker who can stand in for the database server, for example by listening on its port while it is stopped or restarting, to receive the database sign-in, the password included, and to read and modify the traffic between hMailServer and its database. hMailServer applied verify-full by turning the client's certificate verification on without a CA file, but MariaDB Connector/C 3.4.1 and later, on a connection they treat as local and with no CA file, accept any certificate within its validity period that is self-signed or sent with its own root, for any name (Connector/C 3.4.2 to 3.4.10 also one whose issuer they cannot find), so the client accepted the certificate an impostor made, asked no proof of the password and allowed a switch to an authentication method that sends the password unhashed, while hmailserver --check-database said the certificate had been checked against the system's trust store and the application log that it had been checked. problem: Action Pack is a framework for handling and responding to web requests. Prior to 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, When ActionDispatch::Cookies reads a signed or encrypted cookie that was written under a rotated secret (config.action_dispatch.cookies_rotations) or in the format that a:hybrid cookie serializer migrates from, it writes the cookie back to the response in the current format, and that write ignores request.session_options[:skip]. ActiveStorage::DisableSession relies on that option to keep the session cookie off the public, immutable responses of the Active Storage proxy controllers, but those controllers still load the session, so a request carrying an old-format session cookie could receive the rewritten session cookie in Set-Cookie on a cacheable response. A shared cache that stores such a response together with its Set-Cookie header could then serve one user's session to later requesters of the same URL, or serve an attacker's session to other users. Applications are affected when they serve Active Storage files through the proxy controllers, have a cookie rotation or a:hybrid serializer migration configured, and run behind a cache that stores Set-Cookie on public responses. This is a path around the fix for CVE-2024-26144. This issue is fixed in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Strip debug/verbose data and stack traces from responses; restrict sensitive endpoints. Update to the patched version.

problem: Nokogiri is an open source XML and HTML library for the Ruby programming language. From 1.12.0 until 1.19.5, the C extension on CRuby and TruffleRuby has a Nokogiri::HTML5 serializer that does not escape text inside noscript elements or angle brackets inside attribute values. When an application sanitizes untrusted HTML with the default parsing options, allows noscript, and sends serialized output to a scripting-enabled browser, the browser can parse markup that Nokogiri did not produce, enabling mutation cross-site scripting. Using parse_noscript_content_as_text: true is the recommended workaround, not the vulnerable default. JRuby is not affected because it does not implement Nokogiri::HTML5. This issue is fixed in version 1.19.5. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Fixed in version 1.19.5 — update immediately. Encode all user-controlled output, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy, and update to the patched version.

product: Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP
problem: The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP WordPress plugin before 1.70 does not verify that a user may edit a post before letting them change that post's structured data settings, allowing users with the Contributor role and above, when an administrator has granted them access to the Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP WordPress plugin before 1.70, to disable, alter or reset the structured data of posts they do not own. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Enforce per-user ownership checks on every direct object reference. Update to the patched version.

problem: Winter CMS is a content management system built on the Laravel PHP framework. From 1.1.0 until 1.2.14, Backend\Widgets\Lists::evalImageTypeValue() interpolates the result of ImageResizer::filterGetUrl() into a single-quoted image source attribute without escaping it. In a third-party plugin that renders an attacker-influenced value through an image list column, an unsupported image value is returned verbatim, can break out of the attribute, and can inject event handlers that execute when a backend user views the list. Winter core ships no image list column, so a default installation is unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 1.2.14. Exploitable remotely over the network.
solution: Fixed in version 1.2.14 — update immediately. Encode all user-controlled output, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy, and update to the patched version.

problem: The auth0-ai-js FGA retriever does not distinguish between authorization checks under different conditions when filtering documents during retrieval-augmented generation, resulting in documents denied by Auth0 FGA being included in the model context and used in the generated response.
solution: Correct server-side authorization logic and re-test object-level access. Update to the patched version.

problem: The auth0-ai-python FGA retriever does not distinguish between authorization checks under different users, relations, or conditions when filtering documents during retrieval-augmented generation, resulting in documents denied by Auth0 FGA being included in the model context and used in the generated response.
solution: Correct server-side authorization logic and re-test object-level access. Update to the patched version.

problem: The Management API client in the Auth0 Node.js SDK improperly neutralizes path parameters, allowing a request and its attached management API token to be redirected to an unintended endpoint on the same tenant, resulting in unintended access to data or operations that the token's existing scopes already permit.
solution: Canonicalize paths and restrict to an allowlisted directory. Update to the patched version.

problem: The Auth0 ASP.NET Core Authentication SDK incorrectly determines a session's OIDC Back-Channel Logout status, which may result in a logged-out session being accepted for access to protected endpoints.
solution: Enforce authentication on every affected endpoint/server-side; do not rely on client checks. Update to the patched version.

problem: XXE vulnerability in Apache XML Graphics Batik. This issue affects Apache XML Graphics Batik: through 1.19. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.20, which fixes the issue.
solution: Disable external entity resolution in XML parsers. Update to the patched version.

problem: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 5.0.1 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog to store script in entry tags submitted through AtomPub. Roller's tag filter allowed HTML characters in tag names, and the bundled gaurav, fauxcoly and frontpage themes and the showEntryTags macro print tag names without escaping, so the script runs in the browser of anyone who views the weblog. This matters when weblog authors are not trusted with script (weblogAdminsUntrusted=true, the default since 6.1.4). AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes HTML characters from tag names, including names stored earlier.
solution: Encode all user-controlled output, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy, and update to the patched version.

problem: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog that uses a custom theme to store script that runs in the browser of anyone who opens the file's resource URL. The fix for CVE-2026-82387 serves uploaded media as a download unless it is an image, audio, video, PDF or plain text, but media files found through a custom theme were served with the type their path implies, and the upload form let the uploader choose that path. Media uploads are disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which serves these files under the same rules as other media and no longer accepts the path from the upload form.
solution: Encode all user-controlled output, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy, and update to the patched version.

problem: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog member with the Limited role to remove or change entries that member may only read, including entries published by other members. The entry editor checked the member's weblog role but not whether that role permits work on the entry. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later.
solution: Add server-side authorization checks for every object and action. Update to the patched version.

problem: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Roller. When Roller sends a weblog update ping, its XML-RPC client deserializes Java object data contained in the ping target's response, so a party that controls that response can run code in the Roller server process. This issue affects Apache Roller from 4.0 through 6.1.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.7, which removes the unsafe deserialization.
solution: Never deserialize untrusted data; require signed/integrity-checked payloads. Update to the patched version.

problem: The DRPC HTTP endpoint lets an authenticated client act as another user without applying the configured impersonation authorizer. An authenticated user can execute DRPC functions that are restricted to another user. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.0, which fixes the issue.
solution: Correct server-side authorization logic and re-test object-level access. Update to the patched version.

problem: Nimbus returns the worker placement of every topology running on a supervisor, including the host, port, owner and resource assignment of topologies the caller is not authorized to read. In a multi-tenant cluster, an authenticated user who is allowed to access Nimbus can learn where the workers of other users' topologies run. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.2.0, which fixes the issue.
solution: Add server-side authorization checks for every object and action. Update to the patched version.

problem: A Cross-Site Scripting via Unencoded Font Metadata in Apache Batik SVGFont. This issue affects Apache XML Graphics Batik: through 1.19. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.20, which fixes the issue.
solution: Encode all user-controlled output, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy, and update to the patched version.

problem: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache XML Graphics Batik. SVG color-profile xml:base bypasses Batik external resource same-origin checks This issue affects Apache XML Graphics Batik: through 1.19. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.20, which fixes the issue.
solution: Allowlist outbound destination URLs and block internal/metadata IP ranges. Update to the patched version.

problem: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache XML Graphics Batik. This issue affects Apache XML Graphics Batik: through 1.19. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.20, which fixes the issue.
solution: Allowlist outbound destination URLs and block internal/metadata IP ranges. Update to the patched version.

problem: unsafe deserialization in hyphenation loading vulnerability in Apache XML Graphics FOP. This issue affects Apache XML Graphics FOP: through 2.11. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.12, which fixes the issue.
solution: Never deserialize untrusted data; require signed/integrity-checked payloads. Update to the patched version.
